event.name: 2022 Pakistan Monsoon Floods
event.summary: Record monsoon rainfall (PMD: 190% above normal nationally for Jul–Aug; Sindh +726% and Balochistan +590% in August) caused riverine, flash and urban flooding across Pakistan. A national emergency was declared on 25 August 2022.

province_impacts.note: Worst hit: about 70% of total damage and losses (PDNA). Riverine and rain flooding persisted for months.
Flash floods and plains flooding in Jaffarabad and Nasirabad; road links to Sindh cut.
Flash floods on the Swat, Kabul and Indus tributaries; Nowshera and Charsadda evacuated.
Koh-e-Suleman hill torrents hit Dera Ghazi Khan and Rajanpur.
Glacial melt and flash floods; bridges washed away.

incidents.name: Kalam, Swat
incidents.description: The Swat River surge destroyed the multi-storey Honeymoon Hotel and dozens of riverside buildings on the floodplain.

incidents.name: Nowshera
incidents.description: The Kabul River in high flood; authorities ordered the evacuation of large parts of the city.

incidents.name: Rajanpur
incidents.description: Koh-e-Suleman hill torrents inundated villages across Rajanpur and Dera Ghazi Khan.

incidents.name: Dera Allah Yar, Jaffarabad
incidents.description: The plains of eastern Balochistan were submerged and the N-65 link to Sindh was cut for weeks.

incidents.name: Manchar Lake
incidents.description: Pakistan's largest freshwater lake overflowed. Embankment cuts were made to protect Sehwan and Bhan Saeedabad, flooding villages downstream.

incidents.name: Johi, Dadu
incidents.description: The town was ringed by emergency dykes as floodwater surrounded it for weeks.

incidents.name: Jacobabad
incidents.description: UNOSAT detected flood water over about 95% of the district in late August.
